entities.name: Bank of Baroda
entities.label: Institution
entities.summary:
Bank of Baroda is one of India's major public sector banks, founded in 1908 by Maharaja Sayajirao Gaekwad III of the princely state of Baroda (Gujarat). As one of the 14 banks nationalized in 1969 by Indira Gandhi, Bank of Baroda serves as a key pillar of India's public banking system, with a particular international presence in the UK, USA, and East Africa serving the Indian diaspora.

The bank was founded by the enlightened ruler of Baroda — a princely state known for progressive social reform and education investment — as part of a broader modernization program. Sayajirao Gaekwad III, who ruled Baroda 1875-1939, also founded schools, libraries, and supported B.R. Ambedkar's education. The bank's 1908 founding in one of India's most progressive princely states reflects the relationship between Indian nationalism and economic institution-building.

Bank of Baroda's international network, particularly in Uganda and Kenya where it has operated since the 1950s serving Indian diaspora traders, makes it one of Africa's more established Indian banks. The bank merged with Vijaya Bank and Dena Bank in 2019 — the first major bank merger in Indian banking history under the government's public bank consolidation program — creating the third-largest public sector bank in India with 9,500 branches and 84 million customers.
